problem: Existing ImageGoal/Instance ImageGoal navigation methods use a simple Exploration-Exploitation framework and make a one-shot binary match decision from the current observation, so they fail to identify the target instance from a distance and to reject similar distractors.
motivation: IIN requires recognizing the same object instance from different viewpoints while rejecting same-class distractors. Humans 'get closer to confirm' when unsure about distant objects. Matching reliability depends strongly on distance, so the decision should be sequential and distance-aware.
key_idea: Add an active Verification stage between exploration and exploitation, with a switch policy that uses the number of matched keypoints and the agent-to-candidate distance to decide whether to explore, verify (approach) or exploit (confirmed target).
insight: Matching reliability drops sharply with distance (Fig. 7: TP rate collapses at the hard/far level for high thresholds), so a fixed threshold either rejects true targets or accepts false ones. The EVE switch beats a fixed-threshold Exploration-Exploitation policy (Tab. 2: 0.666 vs 0.590 Success with Mask RCNN; 0.684 vs 0.620 with SwinTrans). The GT-perception upper bound of 0.850 shows perception is the remaining bottleneck.
method: Instance Classification: predicts the goal object class from the goal image, either by a Swin Transformer finetuned on HM3D-SEM goal images or by taking the class of the most central instance from the segmentation model.
Online Mapping: Mask RCNN (or InternImage) segments RGB; depth is projected to a voxelized point cloud and scattered into a semantic map, accumulated by max-pooling into a global map.
Local feature matching: DISK keypoints plus LightGlue matching between the goal image and the current observation give the matched keypoint count ω.

Switch Policy f_switch: uses ω, the minimum Euclidean distance d to the same-class potential target, and the segmented depth. It picks exploration, verification or exploitation with distance-dependent upper/lower thresholds, tuned on a self-built instance re-identification dataset.

Goal Mapping Policy: three parallel sub-modules. Exploitation gives the confirmed target as goal map, Verification gives the potential target, and Exploration uses an RL-trained CNN waypoint predictor on the semantic map.
Local Policy: FMM distance field to choose a waypoint and compute the continuous action, plus a visited-trajectory mechanism to avoid getting stuck.

setting.backbone: Modular: Mask RCNN or InternImage segmentation, Swin Transformer classifier (finetuned), DISK+LightGlue matcher, RL exploration CNN (trained from scratch with PPO), FMM local planner
setting.training_data: Only the classifier (HM3D-SEM train goal images) and RL exploration policy (HM3D-SEM train episodes) are trained; the instance re-ID dataset is used to set thresholds; the segmentation models are pretrained (COCO)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (640x480) + sensor pose + goal image (512x512)
setting.action_space: continuous: linear velocity, angular velocity, camera pitch velocity, stop (Habitat Challenge 2023)
setting.privileged: none (GT labels/segmentation only in an upper-bound ablation)

numbers.evidence: Table 1: IEVE Mask RCNN (ours) Success 0.684, SPL 0.241

numbers.extra: RL exploration policy; classifier not stated in Table 1 (Table 2 row 5 uses InternImage for classification)

numbers.method: Ablation: Mask RCNN classification+perception, EVE, RL
Upper bound: GT classification, oracle perception

numbers_note: Metrics are given as fractions (0-1) exactly as printed. Benchmark reported is the Habitat 2023 Instance ImageGoal task on HM3D-SEM; the validation split is used.
results: IEVE achieves 0.684 Success / 0.241 SPL with Mask RCNN and 0.702 / 0.252 with InternImage, beating the previous SOTA Mod-IIN (0.561 / 0.233) and the OVRL-v2 IIN finetune (0.248 / 0.118). The EVE switch beats fixed-threshold EE by about 6-8 Success points.
limitations: Depends heavily on segmentation quality and class labels (GT upper bound 0.850 vs 0.702) and on the RL exploration policy; SPL remains low (~0.25)
Only six object categories are evaluated, and evaluation is on the validation split only in simulation
Keypoint matching becomes unreliable at long range, so hand-tuned distance/threshold switching is required
